issues.issue: The draft-tabs brief tells acquireDraftLock to call navigator.locks.request(name, {ifAvailable: waitMs===0, signal}, cb) and to map 'AbortError → null'. Both parts are wrong (checked in Chromium 1243, scratchpad/1.4/critic2/locks-probe.mjs). (1) {ifAvailable:true, signal} rejects at once: "NotSupportedError: The 'signal' and 'ifAvailable' options cannot be used together". openSession passes its AbortSignal to claim(), and every later claim (File ▸ New, template, Restore, Projects Open, toolbar Join) uses ifAvailable, so every in-editor open fails at claim. (2) AbortSignal.timeout() rejects with 'TimeoutError', not 'AbortError'. The 1500 ms boot wait that should fork a duplicated tab therefore throws, and a caller's abort (supersede or cancel) would be mapped to null and fork instead of cancelling. The unit tests use a fake LockManager and the browser check only covers waitMs 0 without a signal, so none of this is caught before editor-wiring or R13.
issues.fix: In draftLock.ts: when waitMs===0, check opts.signal?.aborted first (throw AbortError if so), then call request(name, {ifAvailable:true}, cb) with NO signal. When waitMs>0, pass signal = AbortSignal.any([AbortSignal.timeout(waitMs), opts.signal].filter(Boolean)). On rejection: if opts.signal?.aborted, rethrow (the open resolves 'cancelled' or 'superseded'); else if err.name === 'TimeoutError', return null (fork plan). withImportLock follows the same rule ('run anyway' on TimeoutError). Make the fake LockManager in the tests throw NotSupportedError for ifAvailable plus signal, and reject with TimeoutError and AbortError respectively. Add a draft-tabs browser check: page A holds the lock, page B calls acquireDraftLock(id, {waitMs:1500, signal}) and must resolve null after about 1.5 s; aborting B's signal must reject with AbortError.

issues.issue: Draft writes are not serialized, so the mirror and an in-flight write can share a writeSeq while holding different content. Both the debounced write and hideFlush use expectedSeq = the committed writeSeq. Sequence: a debounced write W1 (snapshot S1, N→N+1) is in flight when the tab is hidden or closed. hideFlush writes mirror {baseSeq N, writeSeq N+1, S2} and starts W2 (S2, expected N). W1 commits, so W2 hits 'conflict' and the controller forks (spurious copy plus 'changed in another tab' toast) as the page dies. At the next boot IndexedDB has N+1 (S1), and the reconcile rule 'IndexedDB writeSeq ≥ the mirror's writeSeq → drop' throws away S2, the newest edits. This is silent loss on the exact path E5 exists for.
issues.fix: In autosave.ts, keep one write chain per draft (a promise queue). Each write's expectedSeq is the target seq of the write before it. hideFlush sets mirror.baseSeq to the target seq of the last queued write and mirror.writeSeq to baseSeq+1, then queues its strict write behind it. Add contentHash (hashFingerprint of the body text) to DraftMeta and MirrorEntry. Reconcile drops a mirror only when idb.writeSeq > mirror.writeSeq, or when the seqs are equal and the hashes match. With equal seqs and different hashes, create a 'recovered' copy. A CAS conflict whose stored writer.doc === WRITER_DOC (this page) is re-queued on top, never forked. Add a test: hold W1 in a stalled fake transaction, fire pagehide, reload → the mirror content wins and no fork exists.

issues.issue: Mirrors are reconciled only in prepareUser, which is memoized per page and runs before claim(). It skips mirrors whose draft is 'locked elsewhere'. Yet the spec adds a 1500 ms boot wait in claim precisely because the old document can still hold the lock after a refresh; probe-lock-reload.json shows the new document getting it 10–52 ms late. If prepareUser runs inside that window, the tab skips the mirror, then waits for and takes the lock, and opens the stale IndexedDB body. This page's later writes push writeSeq past the mirror's, so the next boot drops the mirror as stale. The previous page's last edits are lost silently, on the R1/R7 path. The window is small, but the fix is cheap and the spec already assumes the lock can be held at boot.
issues.fix: Move the per-draft reconcile into DraftSessionPort.read(claim): right after the lock is acquired (mode 'existing'), reconcile that draft's own mirror under the lock, then read the body. Add a helper reconcileMirror(store, userKey, draftId) to draftMirror.ts. In prepareUser, reconcile only mirrors of unlocked drafts and leave locked ones for the claim. For a fork claim (source still locked by a live tab), leave the source's mirror alone. Add a harness or unit case: a second page holds the draft lock until 800 ms after the new page's prepareUser starts, and the reopened draft must equal the mirror content (R7 idbStalled with a delayed release).

issues.issue: Finishing a media write never schedules a draft write. The draft meta takes media and mediaMissing from pendingMediaManifest() at write time. The autosave triggers are only 1.3's registry triggers, and hideFlush writes only when pendingSeq > committedSeq or viewDirty. After a take, the clip's tracks change triggers the debounced write at about +1 s, while the capture runs a 200 ms debounce, an idle callback of up to 1 s, SHA-256 and a put. The put usually lands after that write. With no further edit, the meta never references the media. On refresh or close the clip has no bytes, so bufferLoaded is lost, and gcMedia deletes the unreferenced blob at the next boot or switch prune once its 10-minute grace has passed. R1, R7 and R23, which expect 'bufferLoaded FIXED', would fail.
issues.fix: In pendingMedia.ts, export onManifestChange(listener) and fire it whenever a put or failure changes the manifest or the missing count. autosave.ts subscribes and calls schedule() (pendingSeq++), so hideFlush and unmount write it. flushOutgoing runs an immediate capture scan (no idle wait) before whenMediaWritesSettled(3000). The harness's waitForDraft also requires media.writing===0 && pendingInMemory===0 and the committed meta's media to equal the manifest.

issues.issue: A draft write during media restore drops the media references. pendingMediaManifest() lists only items whose key→mediaId mapping exists, and restoreDraftMedia registers mappings only after it decodes each ref. restoreMedia runs after ready, while writes are already enabled. Any edit within the first seconds after opening a draft with pending audio (decode can take seconds on a Chromebook) writes meta.media = [] and mediaMissing = N. If the page then closes or crashes, or the restore fails, before another write, gcMedia removes the blobs at the next prune. That is permanent loss of the only copy of the audio. The chip also shows 'Audio not saved yet' during every restore, because missing > 0.
issues.fix: In begin() and apply() for an existing or fork draft, seed pendingMedia synchronously from meta.media before writes resume. Add an export registerDraftMedia(refs) that maps every clipId and samplerSampleId to its mediaId and marks it 'restoring'. The manifest counts restoring and stored items as stored and keeps a ref while its clip or sample still exists in the store. An item becomes missing only when getMedia returns null or decode fails. Add a test: stall restore, make an edit, assert the written meta still lists the ref and the chip is not audio-pending.

issues.issue: E8 ('Takes and drops no longer create cloud projects', and the cloud-save brief's 'return early when store.projectId is null') breaks collaborative audio. Peers hear a recording only through its assetId over Yjs. useCollabAudioLoader.ts says the AudioBuffer store is not synced. Today a take in a room mints a session draft project via ensureProjectId, with roomAtMint → _setSessionDraftProjectId (api.ts:225-255; usePlaybackEngine.ts:405-425; SamplerChopsView.tsx:160). Under 1.4 every collab open resets projectId to null first (?collab=new, host, link joiner, toolbar Join), so takes and sampler drops in a room never upload and peers get silent clips. LeaveSavePrompt's 'delete the session-minted draft' branch also becomes dead.
issues.fix: In upload-pending.ts, skip ensureProjectId only when useStore.getState().roomId is null. In a room, keep today's immediate upload through ensureProjectId (fenced, with roomAtMint), so LeaveSavePrompt's session-draft deletion stays meaningful. Add a cloud-save unit test (a take with roomId set and projectId null calls ensureProjectId and stamps the assetId) and an R19 collabStub flag remoteTakeUploaded.

issues.issue: chooseResume ('pointer, else the newest non-read-only draft') follows updatedAt, which DraftStore.write always sets to now, including for imports. On each user's first 1.4 boot, the legacy import writes L and then up to 5 kept slots (in the brief's order), so the newest draft is a kept slot. A plain /studio/editor then resumes older kept work instead of the student's last session, which looks like 'my work is gone'. A long-lived old tab's 'recovered' import likewise jumps ahead of the user's real draft. On a plain new tab, if the newest draft is locked by another tab, the tab forks it into a '(copy)'. That copy keeps the source's baseline, so it counts as work and lingers for 30 days.
issues.fix: chooseResume: the pointer (same userKey, exists, writable); else the newest unlocked draft with origin in {session, migrated, fork}, ranked by a content time. Exclude kept, recovered and '~device' unless nothing else exists, and fork only for the pointer or duplicated-tab case. Let imports pass their source time: add an optional DraftWrite.updatedAt honoured only when expectedSeq is null and origin is migrated, kept or recovered (data.timestamp, keptAt). Give forks a pristine baseline (current hash, reopenable true) so an unedited fork is a prunable cache. Test: L plus 3 kept slots on first boot resumes L.

issues.issue: The editor-wiring plan wraps the editor content in a display:contents div for inert. src/daw/components/LeadSheet/leadsheet-print.css:32 hides every direct child of .daw-root that is not .leadsheet-container when printing ('.daw-root > *:not(.leadsheet-container) { display:none !important }'). With the wrapper, the wrapper becomes that direct child, gets display:none, and the lead sheet or score prints blank. Verified in Chromium (critic2/inert-probe.mjs): under print media the wrapper computes 'none' and .leadsheet-container has width 0. Inert on display:contents does block focus, so the approach works otherwise. Nothing in R25 or lessons tests printing. The spec also never says the overlay must sit outside the inert subtree; inside it, its Cancel and 'Back to my work' would be dead.
issues.fix: Do not add a wrapper. In a DawApp ref effect, toggle the inert attribute on each direct child of .daw-root except the OpeningHost element while overlay ≠ 'none'. Alternatively, keep the wrapper with class 'daw-content' and assign leadsheet-print.css to editor-wiring with the rule changed to '.daw-root > *:not(.leadsheet-container):not(.daw-content), .daw-content > *:not(.leadsheet-container)'. State that OpeningHost renders outside the inert subtree. Add a check: emulateMedia('print') on Lead Sheet and Score shows .leadsheet-container with non-zero width.

issues.issue: E11's 'Open saved version' action cannot work. After E11 opens the draft, the live session is X and the server is unchanged, so a second {kind:'project', projectId:X} hits 'when the live session already is X and unchanged on the server, do nothing'. From the Projects 'Saved to your account' row, E11 re-picks the same unlocked draft (its cloud.updatedAt equals the server's). The student can never reopen the clean cloud copy while a draft with changes exists, short of deleting the draft.
issues.fix: Add fromCloud?: true to the 'project' OpenIntent (types.ts). With it, openSession skips both the do-nothing rule and findProjectDraft, GETs the project and keeps the live draft under keep:'auto'. The E11 toast action and an 'Open saved version' secondary action on rows tagged changes-on-device pass it. Add openSession tests for both paths.

issues.issue: The storage fallback and missing-record paths are unsafe. (1) After 'two failures' getDraftStore switches the page to the localStorage adapter, even mid-session. The controller's next update to the active draft returns 'not-found' (the draft is not in that adapter), and only conflict, quota and unavailable are handled. When IndexedDB works again on the next load, drafts written during the fallback are never read, so they are orphaned. (2) 'not-found' also happens when another tab's prune, Projects delete or sign-out cleanup removes the active draft: prune('sign-out') and signOutCleanup are not told to protect lockedDraftIds().
issues.fix: Choose the adapter once per page at first open. Later IndexedDB failures set status error 'unavailable' and rely on the mirror, with no adapter switch. At boot, when IndexedDB is available, prepareUser imports any 'musicAtlas:daw:draft:*' adapter records into IndexedDB with the mirror rules. The controller treats 'not-found' on an update as 're-create the same draftId with expectedSeq null, keeping origin and baseline'. signOutCleanup and every prune caller pass protect = lockedDraftIds() ∪ {active}.

issues.issue: The DraftStore.patchMeta contract does not say whether it changes writeSeq or updatedAt. The autosave's lastSaved subscription patches the ACTIVE draft's meta.cloud after every save, and retireOutgoing, claimDeviceDraft and unkeep patch too. An implementation that bumps writeSeq (an easy reading of 'the store sets writeSeq') makes the very next write conflict, so every cloud save forks the session.
issues.fix: Add to the CONTRACTS comment: 'patchMeta never changes writeSeq, writer or the body; it updates updatedAt only for origin, keptAt or name.' Add a draftStore test: write → patchMeta({cloud}) → write with the old expectedSeq succeeds; parameterize it for the localStorage adapter too.

issues.issue: No module is assigned to keep the session's identity in step when the autosave forks on a CAS conflict. The brief says to 'activate it', but activate() only writes the pointer and pauses writes. Nothing acquires the new id's lock, calls begin(), or updates useSessionStore.draftId/userKey. After such a fork, the Projects dialog (activeDraftId, open-now, canDelete), the Continue tile, the rejoin rule (sessionStore.roomId) and deleteDraft's 'refuses the active draft' all point at the old draft, so deleting the live copy is allowed.
issues.fix: Spell out the port's fork path: claim(newId, ifAvailable) → activate → begin(forkBaseline) → release the old lock. Add an exported setter to sessionStore.ts (contracts), adoptActiveDraft(draftId, userKey), and state that only openSession and DraftSessionPort write draftId. deleteDraft checks port.activeDraftId(), not the session store. Add a draftSessionPort test that forces a conflict and asserts the session store, pointer and lock all move.

issues.issue: The spec does not say what happens to an open in flight when the editor unmounts. The sidebar and TopRail stay interactive under the overlay, because only .daw-root is inert. If the student leaves mid-open, the module-scope openSession continues. At ready, deps.navigate (navigate({pathname:'/studio/editor'}, {replace})) yanks them back into the editor and replaces their current history entry, and the toasts and generation-guarded extras run with the editor gone. If DawApp unregisters its deps, getSessionDeps() returns null partway through and behaviour is undefined.
issues.fix: DawApp calls the unregister returned by registerSessionDeps on unmount. In openSession: if deps disappear before keeping, resolve 'cancelled' and release the claim; after the switch, finish without navigate, toasts or overlay timers. deps.navigate is a no-op unless the current location.pathname is '/studio/editor'. Add openSession tests that unregister deps during preparing and during loading.

issues.issue: The single-known-user rule is under-specified, duplicated, and missing an API. (1) Nothing says 'anon' or '~device' do not count as 'another user'. 1.3's startPrefsSync(null) writes musicAtlas:daw:prefs:anon (prefsStore.ts startPrefsSync), and '~device' drafts appear after the first import, so a literal check would send every legacy autosave to '~device' and block the tutorial-progress copy. (2) The rule must also scan 'IndexedDB draft userKeys', but DraftStore has no method to list userKeys. (3) Both draft-tabs (legacyImport) and entry (tutorial progress) implement the same rule, yet entry runs after contracts only and cannot use draft-store, which is a dependency error.
issues.fix: Add knownUserKeys(): Promise<Set<UserKey>> to DraftStore (draft-store). Add one helper to userScope.ts or a new contracts file: otherUserNamespaces(userKey, opts: {store?}) → Set, which excludes 'anon', '~device' and the user's own key and scans the listed localStorage prefixes plus knownUserKeys(). draft-tabs and entry both call it. Make entry depend on draft-store. Persisted per-user stores (tutorial progress, presets) skip writing while getLocalStoreUser() is null.

issues.issue: The spec drifts from 1.3's landed API and re-implements it. saveStatusStore.ts already exports documentSnapshot() and markDocumentBaseline({snapshot, savedComplete}). That ignores a stale snapshot and baselines what the save sent, so an edit made during the PUT reads dirty and undoing it reads clean. It also exports cloudSaveGaps(state, 'legacy'), which already excludes note ids (LEGACY_GAP_NOTE_FIELDS drops 'id') and counts pending media, plus hasWorkToKeep() and isDocumentEmpty(). The 1.4 spec instead has cloud-save build projectHoldsDocumentOnlyData 'from the registry' (note ids are cloud:'document' in NOTE_EVENT_FIELDS, so every project with notes would read incomplete), says to 'skip the baseline if the fingerprint changed' (which loses 1.3's semantics), and adds a second emptyDocFingerprint in snapshot.ts.
issues.fix: List these exports in the CONTRACTS 1.3 header. Set projectHoldsDocumentOnlyData(state) = cloudSaveGaps(state, 'legacy').length > 0, and have documentOnlyGroups map cloudSaveGaps names to the plain group list. saveProject captures documentSnapshot() with the payload and calls markDocumentBaseline({snapshot, savedComplete}) in the same generation. Export 1.3's empty-document fingerprint, or use isDocumentEmpty, for LiveSnapshot.hasContent. The contracts track's reality check verifies all of this.

issues.issue: For most Stage A projects the chip can never read 'Saved', and its 'local' tooltip is wrong right after a save. complete is false whenever the project has chords, a mode other than ionian, a non-4/4 metre, markers, mastering, notation or Prism settings, which covers every demo, song, practice track and most student work. After Cmd-S succeeds, the chip shows 'Saved on this device' with the tooltip 'Press Ctrl+S (⌘S) to save to your account', so students press it again and again. R17's 'retrySaved' does not say which fixture it uses, and a chords fixture can never reach 'saved'.
issues.fix: Add a chip reason 'partial' when lastSaved.projectId===projectId && !lastSaved.complete && content matches: same 'Saved on this device' label and width, tooltip 'Saved to your account. <groups> stay on this device until an update.' R17 offline and retrySaved use a fixture with no document-only data (no chords, ionian, 4/4) and assert data-state 'saved'. A kitchen-sink save asserts 'local' with data-reason 'partial'.

issues.issue: After File ▸ Delete, the draft still points at the deleted project. projectId never bumps documentVersion (fields.ts: 'it never makes the project unsaved'), and setLastSaved(null) does not match the lastSaved→meta.cloud subscription (which patches only when the projectIds are equal). Until the next edit the active draft keeps projectId X and cloud X. Reopening that draft makes 'meta.projectId wins' restore X, and the next save hits 404 and silently re-creates the project the student just deleted, with the 'saved as a new project' toast.
issues.fix: Allow patchCloud(draftId, {projectId: null, cloud: null}). FileMenu Delete calls it on the active draft after the server delete. Save and Save As success also patch projectId, not only cloud. Add a test: delete → reload → session projectId is null and the first save POSTs.

issues.issue: R14 (full: 'a real previous build on :5264') and R15 (revert: 'real builds') need a second build of an earlier commit. The build rules forbid any state-changing git command (so no 'git worktree add'), and the spec gives no recipe. The scenarios track cannot set this up itself, so these Stage-A compatibility gates (old tab plus new tab, and a revert, required by the plan's Verification section) will be skipped or improvised.
issues.fix: Have the integrator provision it before the scenarios track: 'git archive <1.3 commit> | tar -x -C <scratchpad>/prev', symlink node_modules from the main checkout, then 'VITE_CACHE_DIR=<scratchpad>/prev/.vite npx vite --port 5264 --strictPort' with envDir set to the main checkout (per the worktree dev-server note). Pass the base URL to roundtrip as --prev-base. If unavailable, R14-full and R15 report 'skipped', not pass.

issues.issue: The plan's risk section says 'milestones above ~2 weeks ship as flag-guarded sub-PRs'. 1.4 is sized at 3 weeks and grew to 13 tracks, about 30 new modules and 15 new scenario groups, but the spec ships it as one branch and PR with no flag. That drops a plan rule, and one PR makes the harness and scenarios fix loops (which the spec itself calls the long pole) block every other part.
issues.fix: Either split it: 1.4a = drafts, autosave, mirror, legacy import, chip and saveProject over today's boot; 1.4b = openSession, overlay, Song page, File ▸ New in place and Projects dialog, behind a dev flag such as studio.openSession that defaults on only when R11–R25 pass. Or record the owner's explicit waiver in the plan, with an honest week estimate for the harness and scenario loops.

issues.issue: Refused, upgrade and cancelled links stay in the URL. The spec strips 'consumed URL keys' at ready, and on a cold page the follow-up resume consumes only 'seeded'. Today refuse() and the upgrade branch call clearQuery(). Under 1.4 a bad link or a free student's Premium link remains: every refresh re-shows the error or upgrade prompt, and any later location.key change in useSessionBoot re-runs it.
issues.fix: openSession strips the original intent's consumed keys on every terminal outcome (ready, refused, upgrade, failed, cancelled), keeping MSP and utm_* keys. Add a parseBootIntent or openSession test, and assert the URL in R5 and linkGate.

issues.issue: R19 'practiceModeGrooveFails (failAfterResetRestores)' contradicts the prepare/apply split. preparePracticeModeTrack wraps generatePracticeTrack, which does the groove fetch, so a groove failure now happens before keeping and is 'refused', with nothing changed. The flag as named cannot be produced.
issues.fix: Rename it to grooveFailRefusedNothingChanged (expect a panel for a 5xx or offline, or a toast). Cover failAfterResetRestores with a real post-switch failure: a mock fault that makes the project GET return a payload deserializeCloudProject rejects, or the collab stub's join failure.

issues.issue: The spec contradicts itself on how to simulate offline. The risks section says 'offline is a mock fault, not setOffline'; the harness brief says 'an abort fault used together with setOffline'. probe-platform.json shows routed API calls still succeed under setOffline, and E12's single retry waits for the window 'online' event, which only fires on a setOffline true→false flip.
issues.fix: Delete the risks sentence. State: offline = mock abort fault ('internetdisconnected') plus context.setOffline(true), then setOffline(false) to fire 'online'. R17 asserts exactly one PUT after the flip.

issues.issue: Files that no track owns will break when editor-wiring deletes code. src/daw/persistence/__tests__/demoDrums.test.ts imports applyDemoDrums. src/daw/commands/__tests__/RecordGuard.test.tsx vi.mocks '@/daw/collab/ui/WaitingForSessionModal'. Also, Node 24 (vitest 4's default node environment, 'forks' pool) has a real process-wide navigator.locks. Modules that default to navigator.locks will take real locks in tests, so a leaked IMPORT_LOCK or draft lock can stall later files in the same fork. The spec assumes test environments have no locks.
issues.fix: Assign demoDrums.test.ts to entry (port it to prepareDemo/applyDemo) and RecordGuard.test.tsx to editor-wiring (drop the mock). In draftLock.ts and the port, resolve the lock manager through an injectable getter. Test setup uses vi.stubGlobal('navigator', {...navigator, locks: fake}) or passes locks: null.

issues.issue: The chip is fixed at 150 px but has to hold a real Retry button. The measured 'Couldn't save – Retry' text is 107 px at 12 px/400 (save-ui/measure.json). Add a 14 px icon, gaps, chip padding and a 24 px-tall Retry with its own padding, and it reaches 150–160 px, so it can clip.
issues.fix: Fix the layout in the brief: px-2, a 14 px icon, gap-1, and Retry as a text button (min-h-6, px-0, underline). R25 asserts scrollWidth ≤ clientWidth in every state, including error.

issues.issue: E17 settles the sign-out policy (flush, delete reconciled mirrors and cloud-equal drafts, keep unsaved drafts), but the plan lists 'Shared-device policy: what is cleared at sign-out' as an owner item to settle later. Separately, hardLogout's isSessionLogoutInProgressRef guard must be set before 'await runBeforeSignOut', or the burst of 401s during the 1 s flush re-enters it and starts several flushes.
issues.fix: Mark E17 'pending owner sign-off' and add it to the owner walk-through. In AuthContext, set isSessionLogoutInProgressRef.current = true before awaiting runBeforeSignOut(1000).

issues.issue: On the first dashboard visit after deploy, the 'Continue last session' tile disappears. StudioNewProject will read only getDraftStore().list(), and drafts exist only after the editor's legacy import has run, whereas today the tile shows for the legacy autosave. When useSessionStore.draftId is set, the dashboard also has no project name to show, because it may not import the DAW store.
issues.fix: If list() is empty, parse 'musicAtlas:daw:autosave' read-only and link to plain /studio/editor (resume imports it). When draftId is set, read the name with getDraftStore().getMeta(draftId).

issues.issue: A long-lived pre-1.4 tab keeps rewriting 'musicAtlas:daw:autosave', and each boot or Projects open in a new tab imports another 'recovered' draft for every new hash. Each has work and lasts 30 days, so the Projects list fills with near-duplicates; R15's noDuplicateBeyondOne covers only one round. Also, E11 compares server updatedAt, and PATCH /:id/meta (library tags) and asset or cleanup calls likely move it, so 'Changes on this device weren't saved — kept' can fire when the content did not change.
issues.fix: Record legacy source → draftId in the import ledger. When the autosave's hash changes and that draft was never adopted (origin migrated or recovered, no later writes), CAS-update it instead of creating another. For E11, compare Date.parse values and treat 'server newer' as conflicting only when the GET's tracks or settings differ from the draft's cloud fingerprint, or document the false positive until 1.5's revision.

issues.issue: Two smaller gaps. Tutorial progress 'rehydrate on onLocalStoreUserChange' leaks across users: zustand 5's default persist merge keeps the current in-memory state when the new key holds nothing (node_modules/zustand/middleware.js hydrate), so the previous user's completedAt carries into a user with no key and is written under their name on the next markComplete. And __COMMIT_SHA__, which the store's writer.build uses, is defined in vite.config.ts but declared nowhere in src, so tsc fails.
issues.fix: On a user change: set({completedAt: legacyCopyOrEmpty}), then persist.setOptions({name}) and rehydrate with merge: (p, c) => ({...c, completedAt: p?.completedAt ?? c.completedAt}); test an in-page A→B switch. In draftStore.ts add 'declare const __COMMIT_SHA__: string | undefined' and read it behind a typeof guard (default 'dev').
